description: We are Shine My Way, a team of 5 secondary school students from Hanoi, Vietnam, guided by our science teacher. We love space, science and solving real problems. We are working on an interplanetary survival guide with a map of Mars. We combine research, design and basic coding to turn NASA data into something everyone can understand. We welcome anyone who can help with coding, graphic design or presenting in English!
summary: We created SMW using AI, NASA data, and many other sources. We turned this software into a fun experience with clear 3D space visuals and useful facts. It solves the problem of hard-to-read data by giving users clear pictures and exact details so they can understand easily. This is important because it gives people quick, simple answers without needing to search through thousands of long reports.
details:
We created SMW, a web software that shows places on Earth that are like Mars and the Moon. It helps users find the best spots on Earth to test space shelters and rocket launch pads. This project works by turning complex data into fun experiences with clear 3D visuals and useful facts.
Benefits & Expected Impact
SMW solves the problem of hard-to-read data by giving users clear pictures and exact details. This is important because it gives quick, simple answers without needing to search through thousands of long reports. In the future, we expect SMW to bring exciting learning experiences to more users and grow into a large community.
Tools & Technology
We use AI technology, NASA data, and many other data sources to build this web software.
Creativity & Team Considerations
Our project is creative because we use realistic 3D visuals to explain facts, helping users imagine these places more clearly. Our team focused on creativity and shared complete information that closely follows the challenge.
dataRefs: SHINE MY WAY – NASA Data: NSSDCA Planetary Fact Sheets (Earth, Moon, Mars), NASA Mars Trek, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO/LROC), Artemis, Haughton-Mars Project, NASA Astrobiology, Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity), Mars 2020 (Perseverance), Apollo 11, NASA/JPL Photojournal
